unreg:combine_testing_results.target: Probability that the best Combine result in a drill (fastest 40-yard dash, longest broad jump, highest vertical jump, most bench-press reps at 225 lb) clears a threshold, belongs to a named prospect, or (for the 40) belongs to a named position, per official Combine results.
unreg:combine_testing_results.mechanism: Combine drill extremes are the maximum (broad jump, vertical jump, bench-press reps) or minimum (40-yard dash) over the prospects who are invited AND choose to perform the drill in Indianapolis. The outcome is generated in three layers: the invite pool and its position mix fix how many genuine speed and explosiveness candidates exist, at any position; each prospect's opt-in decision (injury, agent strategy, deferral to pro day) thins that pool, often removing the favourite; each participant's best-of-attempts result is his trained athletic ceiling plus attempt noise measured by the Combine's timing protocol. A threshold beyond the all-time record or an argmax among near-equal sprinters is therefore a tail and participation problem, not a draft-board problem. The vertical shares the jumpers and opt-out behaviour of the broad jump but has its own prior; the bench press is a separate lineman-driven pool; and the position-of-fastest-40 market is the same argmax summed over each runner's position group, so it must come from one joint simulation with the player market.
contract_types: Pro Football Draft Combine: Longest Broad Jump
Pro Football Draft Combine: Player with Fastest 40 Time
Pro Football Draft Combine: Highest Vertical Jump
Pro Football Draft Combine: Most Bench Press Reps
Pro Football Draft Combine: Position with Fastest 40 Time

attach.why: Yearly best 40, broad jump, vertical and bench-press reps, and the record for each, anchor the order-statistic tail of each drill, including the 148-inch broad-jump strike.

A named prospect only wins the fastest-40 market (player or position), or sets a jump or rep mark, if he performs that drill at the Combine; opt-outs of fast or explosive prospects reshape each drill's argmax, and the two jumps are usually skipped or performed together.

College track times, verified sprint data, jump marks and size give each participant's expected 40 time and broad jump before he tests; the vertical and the bench press have their own priors (nfl.combine_vertical_jump_prior, nfl.combine_bench_press_pool_and_prior).

Stage s3 yield for quarterbacks and their stacks: the starter's EPA+CPOE prior sets yards per attempt and touchdown rate, which convert dropbacks into passing fantasy points (0.04 per yard, 4 per touchdown) and into the quarterback-receiver covariance of the aggregation stage.

Stage s3 opponent matchup: position-specific yards, receptions and touchdowns allowed per target or carry adjust each RB, WR and TE's per-opportunity yield; its incremental value over role and script is unmeasured (u3).
Stage s3 matchup: the opponent's man/zone and single-high/two-high mix shifts targets between WR and TE/RB and short versus deep, changing full-PPR reception count and yardage yield per target.

Stage s3 environment for the single-game KXNFLFFPTS, ladder, weekly-leader and any-game tickers: kickoff-hour wind, precipitation and cold cut passing and kicking yield and raise run share, taken as forecast vintages to avoid look-ahead.

unreg:slate_extremes.target: Probability that the maximum (or argmax) of a per-game quantity (game margin, game total, team points, or a single player's single-game or single-quarter stat: rushing, passing and receiving yards, receptions, touchdowns, sacks, tackles, interceptions, D/ST touchdowns, rushing-plus-receiving 100/100) across a week's or season's slate of games exceeds a threshold or falls on a named game/team.
unreg:slate_extremes.mechanism: Each contract reads the extreme of one per-game quantity over a set of games: the season's largest final margin, largest total including overtime, the largest single-game stat of any player (rushing, passing or receiving yards, receptions, touchdowns, sacks, tackles, interceptions, D/ST touchdowns) or single-quarter yardage (overtime excluded), or which game or team scores most in one week. The extreme is produced by the few games with the most lopsided talent pairings, quarterback absences, calm conditions for totals (dome or mild weather) and, for margins, any weather since bad conditions can widen mismatches and runaway scripts (turnover cascades, defensive touchdowns, a leader that keeps scoring). Player legs are maxima over every player-game of the season: they come from concentrated volume and high variance (a lead back with 25-35 carries in a winning script, a quarterback in a high-total game, a high-target receiver, a pass rusher against a weak line) and from Poisson-like counts with heavy right tails for touchdowns, sacks, tackles and interceptions, and are only weakly tied to the game margin. Probability is one minus the product of per-game non-exceedance over remaining games for season thresholds, with shared team-rating error adding dependence; for weekly argmax it is a simulation over the slate's integer score distributions with dead-heat splitting.

attach.why: Stage s7 receiving legs (receiving yards 250-300, receptions 15-20, receiving and 100/100 rungs): the top-target receiver's target share and depth set the volume from which the player-stat extreme family draws its reception and yardage tails.

team_total.mechanism: Team points = team possessions x points per possession, built from the team's own market-free inputs: its offence efficiency against the opponent's defence, pace and clock control (possessions), red-zone and kicker finishing, QB/OL/skill availability and weather. The distribution is a right-skewed discrete score pmf with clusters at multiples of 3 and 7 (nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean) that is positively dependent on the opponent's score through shared pace, weather and script (nfl.paired_score_covariance_own); each rung is read from that pmf per the overtime wording. Sportsbook game totals, spreads and implied splits are benchmarks to compare against, never inputs to the team mean.

attach.why: Interaction with opponent pass defence and own EPA: a pass-heavy offence's points are hurt more by a strong pass defence and a run-heavy one's by run defence; pass rate over expected also sets the play mix feeding the drive-result lattice.

Stage t7 (KXNFLBOTH, each team at least N points, overtime included): the joint upper tail P(home>=N, away>=N) is read from this per-bin Student-t copula, so it owns the tail dependence rather than supplying context; calibration at N = 28-42 against empirical joint frequencies is untested (u5).

Stage t7 marginals: each team's OT-inclusive integer score pmf, with the key-number mass at 3, 6, 7, 10 and 14, is the marginal over which the paired copula is applied to obtain the both-at-least-N tail.

Stage t6: points and probability added to a full-game total by overtime under each rule era, quantifying either reading of the silent contract text; the 2025+ both-possess increment is unverified beyond secondary reports.

Stages t6 and t7 and the settlement coverage: overtime frequency, rule era and tie probability decide whether a regulation tie adds points to the total and to a both-teams-at-least-N outcome; the rule era in force for 2026 is not verified from a primary source.

Strike construction (N+ half-point floors), the 2-point-try sack exclusion in KXNFLTEAMSACK, the 48-hour postponement clause and the regular-season window come from the sampled rules text; overtime treatment, data source and both-team postponement are unstated in it.

Regular-season window, counted object (tied games; made field goals from at least 60 yards) and strike come from the sampled rules text; source of truth, kick-distance definition and treatment of unplayed games are unstated.
Coverage shell x target distribution interaction: which receivers see targets, and how deep, converts a defensive coverage shell into the quarterback's yards per attempt.
Stage q2 pass-attempt volume: neutral-situation pace sets plays per game and thereby the dropbacks over which touchdown passes and interceptions accrue.
Teammate injury x target competition interaction: absence of the WR1 or a back redistributes targets to replacements with different per-target efficiency.
Stage s2: plays per game scale the team pass attempts available to be targeted.
Stage s8 rushing-plus-receiving sums and running-back role: carry share and passing-down role decide the rushing half of combined yards and the receptions a back is used for.
Talent_strength coverage: team offence strength sets the pool of touchdowns from which first-scorer and anytime shares are drawn.
The halftime-state mixture for Q3, Q4 and 2H contracts takes its first-half projection from the model margin lattice (see nfl.halftime_margin_scoring_model measurement).
Official practice and game designations are fed through the weather and lineup vintages dataset and determine availability of quarterbacks, kickers and pass rushers behind the event rates.
